quotes.text: AI amplifies drift, it doesn't heal it. Models learn from artifacts. If intent is implicit and scattered, AI infers policy from stale templates, inconsistent labels and noisy histories.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why AI pilots in HR expose rather than fix scattered policy.

quotes.text: Access is not a derivative of personhood, it's a derivative of risk, obligation and capability, those change outside HR.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes identity as its own control plane instead of a mirror of HR data.

quotes.text: The illusion is that auditability equals explainability. Workday can show you who approved what when and along which path. It cannot by itself show the clause of policy that required the path.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Separates process audit trails from provable policy enforcement.

quotes.text: In a healthy architecture Power Automate is a transport and coordination layer, in an unhealthy one it's the brain. You don't fix that by writing better flows, you fix it by moving policy out of flows.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear architectural rule for where automation should and should not hold policy.

takeaways: Hire-to-retire is not a linear process but a stream of facts, obligations and identity changes processed by many systems that make independent decisions.
Policy hidden in templates, stages, connector conditions, flows and Conditional Access exceptions creates configuration entropy that AI will mirror instead of fix.
A four-layer architecture with a versioned policy layer, immutable events, subscriber-only execution and an explanation-first AI layer lets HR own intent while platforms execute and Entra enforces.
hook: HR platforms promise a clean hire-to-retire lifecycle, yet policy ends up scattered across templates, workflows, Power Automate flows and Entra exceptions until nobody can explain why someone still has access. This episode is for HR, identity and platform architects working with Dynamics 365 HR, Workday, SuccessFactors and Microsoft 365, and it delivers a diagnostic checklist, a reference architecture and a 90-day plan to make HR systems explainable and ready for AI.
